## Import and Preview the Dataset

Run the code below to import the teaching dataset and view the first few rows.

```{webr-r}
drinking_data <- read.csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhengyangzhou/moodle-webr2/main/data/college_drinking_long.csv"
)

head(drinking_data)
```

## Check the Dataset Size

Use `dim()` to see the number of rows and columns.

```{webr-r}
dim(drinking_data)
```

You can also check the number of rows and columns separately.

```{webr-r}
nrow(drinking_data)
ncol(drinking_data)
```

## View the Variable Names

Use `names()` to see all variables in the dataset.

```{webr-r}
names(drinking_data)
```

## Examine the Dataset Structure

Use `str()` to see how R has interpreted each variable.

```{webr-r}
str(drinking_data)
```

## Get a Quick Summary

Use `summary()` to obtain a general overview of the variables.

```{webr-r}
summary(drinking_data)
```

## Examine Categories and Assessment Times

Use `table()` to count the observations in selected variables.

```{webr-r}
table(drinking_data$month)

table(drinking_data$treatment)

table(drinking_data$study_id)
```

## Compare Study and Treatment Groups

A two-way table can show which treatment groups are represented within each study.

```{webr-r}
table(drinking_data$study_id,
      drinking_data$treatment)
```

## Check Data Quality

First, examine the `mandated` variable.

```{webr-r}
table(drinking_data$mandated)
```

Then check whether any variables contain missing values.

```{webr-r}
colSums(is.na(drinking_data))
```
